literal: Even if one has not learned, let him listen; that, to a person, in times of weakness, will be a supporting staff.
translation: Even if a person has not learned through formal study, let them listen to the wise; in times of weakness and distress, that acquired knowledge will serve as a steadying staff.
modern: ஒருவர் நூல்களைக் கற்கவில்லை என்றாலும், கற்றறிந்தவர்களின் சொற்களைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்; அப்படிக் கேட்பது அவருக்குத் தளர்ச்சி வரும் காலத்தில் ஊன்றுகோல் போன்ற துணையாக இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of listening as a source of wisdom, especially for those who lack formal education. Even if a person has not studied books, they should actively listen to the words of the wise. In times of mental or physical weakness and vulnerability, the wisdom gathered through listening acts like a sturdy staff that prevents them from falling. The metaphor of the supporting staff beautifully illustrates how oral learning provides stability and guidance during life's difficult moments.
